title: Observability: privacy provenance & access-audit workflow for traces/logs/metrics
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Implement end-to-end workflow to enforce privacy, provenance, and access auditing for telemetry (traces, logs, metrics) across ingestion pipelines and dashboards. Goals: 1) reliably remove or pseudonymize PII at ingress while preserving trace correlation and latency/error dashboards; 2) implement per-team retention policies and resource-scoped RBAC; 3) create immutable access audit trail for any accesses to raw telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress processors redact or pseudonymize fields matching PII schema while preserving trace/span IDs
All playback of full raw payloads requires explicit RBAC grant and generates audit log entries
Per-project retention windows configurable via Console and enforced in storage lifecycle jobs
Latency and error dashboards remain functional and match pre-governance baselines within 5% of prior metrics
implementation_plan: Add OTel processor chain in ingestion for configurable remove/hash/kms-wrap actions
Introduce telemetry schema registry with PII-tags and provenance metadata
Enhance storage lifecycle job to enforce retention windows and tombstone policy
Extend Console RBAC to gate 'view raw telemetry' with audit recording and short-lived access tokens
Ship canary in staging > dedicated > hosted; monitor regressions via synthetic traces
decision_record: Use deterministic hashing (HMAC with per-customer salt) for correlation-safe pseudonymization instead of full redaction to preserve joinability across traces
Keep high-cardinality fields hashed rather than removing to avoid metric cardinality explosions
Sensitive raw payloads encrypted at rest using KMS + HSM-backed keys and moved to restricted S3 bucket with separate billing tags
Run primary redaction at the edge/ingress for latency-critical customer tiers; for Dedicated/Private deployments allow configurable in-cluster processors
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial kickoff with product and security; agreed on scope and success metrics (traces/logs/metrics)
2026-03-04: Prototype OTel processor chain (remove/hash/kms-wrap) implemented in staging; added unit tests for common PII patterns
2026-03-06: Spike comparing HMAC vs tokenization for correlation; HMAC chosen for lower operational friction
2026-03-07: Design review with Console team; RBAC gating UX wireframes added to drive (https://drive.redwood.ai/obs-governance/wireframes)
2026-03-08: Security feedback: require KMS access audit, key rotation guidance, and threat model update (see Confluence https://confluence.redwood.ai/obs/privacy-provenance)
2026-03-09: Storage lifecycle job prototype to tombstone raw payloads after retention window; metrics rollups retained longer
2026-03-10: Load test showing ingress redaction adds 2-5ms p95 on standard traces; acceptable for hosted P1 customers but need opt-out for ultra-low-latency tiers
2026-03-11: Drafted readiness checklist and e2e test plan; created GH issue tracking PRs (https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pulls/452)
2026-03-12: Started Console RBAC implementation; created audit log schema and sample events (see dashboard prototype https://app.redwood.ai/dashboards/obs-audit-proto)
risks: Potential increased ingestion latency for high-throughput tenants; mitigation: selective ingress sampling and deferred heavy redaction for non-P1 tiers
Hashing preserves joinability but could enable correlation attacks if salts leaked; mitigation: per-customer salts rotated and KMS-protected
Retention enforcement bug could prematurely delete data; mitigation: staging-only soft-delete and dry-run retention reporter before full rollout
next_steps: Complete PRs for OTel processor and storage lifecycle (PR#452 and 458)
Finish Console RBAC gating and integrate audit logging
Run cross-team tabletop with Security and Privacy
Schedule canary release for a subset of hosted customers and Dedicated staging clusters
